[EFFECT]
The weekday feature has a non-monotonic, categorical effect — each day of the week produces its own distinct pattern of contributions rather than a simple rising or falling trend. Sunday (0) stands out with a strongly negative central tendency (SHAP values reaching as low as −0.9), suggesting demand is pulled down on Sundays relative to the average. Mid-week days (Monday through Friday, values 1–5) tend to cluster in positive territory (roughly +0.2 to +0.3 at their core), indicating a demand boost on workdays. Saturday (6) behaves similarly to Sunday, with a wide spread of both positive and negative values, reflecting that certain hours boost demand (leisure riding) while others suppress it.

[IMPORTANCE]
Weekday is the 4th most important feature out of 9, making it a moderately strong driver of predicted demand — clearly influential, though less so than the top three features.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Plan for higher baseline bike availability on weekdays (Monday–Friday) compared to Sunday, while on weekends staffing and redistribution should be timed to specific leisure-peak hours rather than assuming a flat daily pattern.
